This harness has no literal '/export' command, so this record was compiled from the actual conversation and the committed planning/implementation artifacts rather than produced by a command. No secrets are included; any transient tokens from earlier inherited context were never written here.

project.name: Review Impact Analysis (RIA)
project.tagline: Close the loop on negative feedback
project.framing: An Experience.com / XMP review-intelligence capability, demoed on the restaurant vertical (not a generic restaurant app).
project.problem: Multi-location brands collect reviews easily, but turning a location's 1-2 star reviews into a specific fix and then proving the fix worked is manual, slow, and inconsistent.
project.solution: A closed-loop MVP: detect problems, benchmark peers on the same item, contrast positive peer reviews, derive a beyond-classification root cause, recommend a specific remedy, track the action, then render a before/after verdict and, on failure, the next remedy.
project.architecturePrinciple: Business/analysis logic lives only in pure services (no React/antd/store imports, enforced via ESLint). Pages call services; the mock service bodies can be swapped for real Experience.com XMP AI behind identical typed signatures without touching the UI.
project.determinism: No Math.random/Date.now/new Date; a single seeded PRNG (mulberry32); hardcoded ISO dates; authored ground-truth tags; nothing computed is persisted.

workflow.phase1_requirements: Product agent first; then UX, Data, Analysis in parallel (depend on Product); then Frontend (needs UX + Data) and QA (needs Data + Analysis).
workflow.phase2_review: Tech-Lead reads all six plans, resolves conflicts (e.g. component count, verdict-vs-status wording, remedyTable location), audits coverage, produces architecture-review.md.
workflow.phase3_implementation_planning: Tech-Lead synthesizes implementation-plan.md (phases, tasks, dependencies, files, validation); implementation then proceeds phase by phase with tsc + build checks after each phase.
workflow.dependencies: Product -> UX/Data/Analysis; UX+Data -> Frontend; Data+Analysis -> QA; all -> Tech-Lead review -> implementation-plan.

prompts.title: Master planning prompt
prompts.prompt: Act as Lead Architect for an MVP called Review Impact Analysis. Do NOT implement code yet. First create a complete implementation plan using a multi-agent/agentic workflow. Product objective: help restaurant owners understand what customers are unhappy about, why, how they compare to peers, what successful restaurants do differently, what remedy to take, what action to perform, and whether the action improved feedback. Core flow: Reviews -> Detect Problems -> Analyze -> Peer Comparison -> Positive Review Comparison -> Root Cause -> Remedy -> Action Plan -> Owner Takes Action -> Collect New Reviews -> Before/After Analysis -> Measure Improvement -> Confirm Improvement OR Recommend Next Remedy. Tech stack: React + TypeScript + Vite, Ant Design v4, styled-components, Recharts, Zustand, React Router, mock data, localStorage, no backend, mock AI. Separate business logic from UI (services). Produce product-plan, ux-plan, data-plan, analysis-plan, frontend-plan, qa-plan, architecture-review, and implementation-plan.

prompts.title: Per-agent authoring (shared authoritative context)
prompts.prompt: Each planning agent reads one shared source-of-truth spec (fixed names, types, routes, 13 categories, 6 action statuses, the 6 pages, the 23 components, the before/after mechanism, the pure-services rule, the deterministic seeding rules) and authors exactly one planning document from its perspective, using the exact names verbatim so the documents stay mutually consistent.

prompts.title: Implementation kickoff
prompts.prompt: The planning phase is approved. Start implementation. Follow the agreed architecture, resolve the known planning conflicts, start with Phase 1, and implement the MVP phase by phase. After each phase run TypeScript checks and the production build and fix errors. Keep UI and business logic separate; use only the agreed tech stack; use mock data and mock AI only; no backend or real AI. Keep the demo scenarios working: Scenario 5 must PASS (Improvement Confirmed), Scenario 6 must FAIL and recommend the next remedy.

prompts.title: First working flow (priority)
prompts.prompt: Build and validate the complete flow end to end: Login -> Dashboard -> Negative Review -> Analysis -> Peer Comparison -> Root Cause -> Remedy -> Action -> Before/After -> Improvement. Then report what was built, files changed, build status, test status, blockers, and the next step.

prompts.title: Expand the mock dataset
prompts.prompt: Keep exactly 10 users and 10 restaurants. Increase reviews to 20-30 per restaurant (200-300 total) and 20-30 shared menu items. Create realistic, meaningful review patterns (not random) covering all 13 categories, with some restaurants better than others per category, shared items for peer comparison, positive peer reviews for every major negative, dates across the last 90 days, and the existing before/after data preserved. Do not change UI or business logic. Validate counts and run TypeScript + production build.
